messages.subject: power simulation multiple groups
parts:
Hi,

I am not very knowledgeable about power analysis/simulation but am trying to conduct a power analysis before wave 2 data are collected to submit a registered report (so have very little time). I would therefore be extremely grateful for any advice. 

I want to conduct a power analysis simulation for a multiple (6) group structural equation model with varying group sizes. I am interested in power for the parameters so my approach has been to set small effects in the population but equal across groups (though non-invariance is plausible).

I have been using the sim() function from simsem. I notice that when I manually specify the above scenario writing group: 1 etc. in the lavaan syntax  and in this example https://github.com/simsem/simsem/blob/master/SupportingDocs/Examples/Version05/ex6/ex6.R
the constrained across groups models do not provide coverage and bias for summaryParam(Output, detail = T). In the link above, I think the configural model does produce coverage/bias.

Is it possible to get power, coverage and bias for constrained parameters across groups or is this the wrong approach?

many thanks in advance,

Louise

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: power simulation multiple groups
parts:
The reason that example doesn't have automatic calculations of bias, etc., is because it uses rawData= instead of a data-generating function/syntax in the model= argument.  It should not be necessary to use rawData=; just specify your population parameters explicitly in the lavaan syntax or the SimSim model objects.  Then the population parameters you specify will be available in the SimResult object, so summaryParam() will be able to automatically calculate bias, etc.

FYI, to use variable sample sizes across replications in a multigroup setting, you need to pass a list of integer-vectors to n=.  Each list element corresponds to 1 group, and each integer in the group's vector represents the sample size of that group in replication [i].  Thus, each list element needs the same length().  So for 5 replications of 3 groups, each with a random N between 50 and 100, it would look like this.

set.seed(123)
ngroups <- 3
nReps <- 5
MyNs <- lapply(1:ngroups, function(g) sample(50:100, size = nReps))

[[1]]
[1] 80 64 63 52 91

[[2]]
[1] 99 92 86 63 74

[[3]]
[1] 75 76 54 99 77
